query: Consider the following context: Materials capable of withstanding extreme environments open promising opportunities for nuclear fusion reactors. In that context, which material can be used for interlayer materials between W and CuCrZr, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tungsten carbide (WC) can be used as an interlayer material between tungsten (W) and CuCrZr due to its high thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, and compatibility with both materials.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 5-10 μm thick tungsten carbide (WC) interlayer
generation.mechanism: Thermal conductivity and mechanical strength of WC enable efficient heat transfer and reduce thermal stress between W and CuCrZr
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20-30% increase in thermal conductivity and a 15-25% reduction in thermal stress at the W-CuCrZr interface compared to the baseline (without interlayer)
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the WC interlayer may vary depending on the deposition method, crystal structure, and impurity levels

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare W-CuCrZr samples with and without WC interlayer, and measure thermal conductivity and thermal stress under high-temperature and high-vacuum conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured thermal conductivity increase is less than 10% or the thermal stress reduction is less than 5%, the hypothesis is falsified
